answer: DeepWalk’s reported performance suggests that, under sparse supervision, **homophily-based similarity**—that is, nodes being similar because they are close in the graph and tend to share labels or community membership—is especially useful. In contrast, node2vec’s BFS/DFS bias is meant to trade off between local homophily and more structural/role-based similarity, but DeepWalk’s strong results indicate that simple random-walk neighborhoods capturing local proximity are often enough when labeled data are scarce.
